column1: # Known Layer-3 failures: comparisons that breach the blocking threshold because
# of a filed, open defect in ltl — not because the harness is miscalibrated.
# An entry suppresses the block for exactly one (scenario, file_kind, column,
# key_class) combination and is reported as XFAIL, with its issue, on every run.
# It is NOT a tolerance: the comparison still happens and the deviation is still
# printed.
# Entries are self-clearing. If a registered comparison PASSES, the engine fails
# the run with "known failure no longer reproduces" — so the fix cannot land
# without the entry being removed in the same change.
# Columns:
#   scenario    — scenario id from scenarios.tsv
#   file_kind   — messages | stats
#   column      — the CSV column whose comparison is expected to breach
#   key_class   — merged (row key contains the consolidation wildcard '*')
#                 | any
#   issue       — the open defect this is waiting on
#   note        — why, in one line
# #459: combining two bin-counter histograms re-projects both sides onto a
# union geometry by geometric midpoint. The displacement compounds with merge
# depth, so a cluster's percentiles drift from the true sample set. Measured
# against the oracle on 2026-08-26: percentiles 2.7-4.2%, IQR to 32.6% (IQR is
# a difference of two percentiles, so it carries both errors). Only the two
# deep-merge scenarios breach; apache-bin-consolidated, at 52 projections,
# stays inside the threshold. The raw *-consolidated scenarios agree exactly,
# which is what identifies the bin merge as the cause rather than the grouping.
# D1 in features/bin-counter-accuracy-and-observability.md is the fix: project
# each member once, from pristine counts, at finalize. When it lands these
# entries must be deleted, and the engine will insist on it.
